title: The Slow Route, and Where the Map Stops

scenes.visual: Title card: The Slow Route, and Where the Map Stops.

scenes.tts: Freezing begins while the tone still plays. So why does the hormone peak only tens of minutes later?
scenes.visual: A fast clock beside a freezing rat, and a slow clock beside a hormone droplet. Title card: The slow route, and where the map stops.
scenes.narration: Freezing begins while the tone still plays. So why does the hormone peak only tens of minutes later?

scenes.tts: Because it runs through three relays: hypothalamus, pituitary, adrenal.
scenes.visual: A chain of three boxes from top to bottom: hypothalamus, pituitary, adrenal. Label: H P A axis.
scenes.caption: Because it runs through three relays: hypothalamus, pituitary, adrenal.
scenes.narration: Because it runs through three relays: hypothalamus, pituitary, adrenal.

scenes.tts: Neurons in the hypothalamus release C R H into tiny vessels that lead to the pituitary.
scenes.visual: The top box releases dots labelled CRH into short portal vessels running down the pituitary stalk.
scenes.caption: Neurons in the hypothalamus release CRH into tiny vessels that lead to the pituitary.
scenes.narration: Neurons in the hypothalamus release CRH into tiny vessels that lead to the pituitary.

scenes.tts: The pituitary answers by releasing A C T H into the general circulation.
scenes.visual: The middle box releases dots labelled ACTH into a wide blood vessel.
scenes.caption: The pituitary answers by releasing ACTH into the general circulation.
scenes.narration: The pituitary answers by releasing ACTH into the general circulation.

scenes.tts: A C T H reaches the adrenal cortex, which makes cortisol, or corticosterone in rats.
scenes.visual: The bottom box: the outer layer of the adrenal gland lights up and releases droplets labelled cortisol (corticosterone in rats).
scenes.caption: ACTH reaches the adrenal cortex, which makes cortisol, or corticosterone in rats.
scenes.narration: ACTH reaches the adrenal cortex, which makes cortisol, or corticosterone in rats.

scenes.tts: The pituitary answers within minutes. But the adrenal must make its hormone, so levels peak tens of minutes later.
scenes.visual: A timeline under the chain: an ACTH trace rises within minutes; the glucocorticoid trace rises after a lag and peaks later. Label: synthesis sets the slow clock.
scenes.narration: The pituitary answers within minutes. But the adrenal must make its hormone, so levels peak tens of minutes later.

scenes.tts: As the hormone rises, it feeds back and turns down further release. A low baseline carries on.
scenes.visual: An arrow curves from the adrenal back up to the pituitary and the brain, marked with a minus sign. The hormone trace settles toward a continuing low baseline, not to zero.
scenes.narration: As the hormone rises, it feeds back and turns down further release. A low baseline carries on.

scenes.tts: This thermostat has two speeds. A fast arm acts over seconds to minutes.
scenes.visual: A thermostat icon with two dials. The fast dial turns. Label: fast, nongenomic.
scenes.narration: This thermostat has two speeds. A fast arm acts over seconds to minutes.

scenes.tts: A slow arm works by changing which genes are read, over hours to days.
scenes.visual: The slow dial turns. A receptor moves into a cell nucleus. Label: delayed, genomic.
scenes.narration: A slow arm works by changing which genes are read, over hours to days.

scenes.tts: Even with no threat at all, the hormone rises and falls. It has a daily rhythm, and pulses about once an hour.
scenes.visual: A long trace over a day: one broad daily wave with small hourly pulses riding on it.
scenes.narration: Even with no threat at all, the hormone rises and falls. It has a daily rhythm, and pulses about once an hour.

scenes.tts: Is each hourly pulse a command from the hypothalamus?
scenes.visual: The hourly pulses are highlighted, with a question mark pointing back to the hypothalamus box.
scenes.narration: Is each hourly pulse a command from the hypothalamus?

scenes.tts: Walker and colleagues tested this in rats. They chose a time of day when the rat's own C R H is low. So new pulses were unlikely to be the rat's own commands.
scenes.visual: Card: Walker and colleagues, 2012. A rat corticosterone trace, flat at the daily low point.
scenes.caption: Walker and colleagues tested this in rats. They chose a time of day when the rat's own CRH is low. So new pulses were unlikely to be the rat's own commands.
scenes.narration: Walker and colleagues tested this in rats. They chose a time of day when the rat's own CRH is low. So new pulses were unlikely to be the rat's own commands.

scenes.tts: Then they dripped in C R H at a perfectly steady rate. If every pulse is a command, what should you see?
scenes.visual: A constant-rate pump icon feeds a flat input line. Question card over the empty output trace.
scenes.caption: Then they dripped in CRH at a perfectly steady rate. If every pulse is a command, what should you see?
scenes.narration: Then they dripped in CRH at a perfectly steady rate. If every pulse is a command, what should you see?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: Commands alone would give a steady, raised level. Instead, the hormone still rose and fell, about once an hour.
scenes.visual: Under the flat input line, the output trace draws peaks and troughs about an hour apart. Label: about 0.89 pulses per hour.
scenes.narration: Commands alone would give a steady, raised level. Instead, the hormone still rose and fell, about once an hour.

scenes.tts: So in this preparation, pulsed C R H was not needed. Given a steady infusion, the pituitary and adrenal loop can make its own rhythm.
scenes.visual: A separate intravenous pump labelled: constant CRH infusion, 0.5 µg/h, feeds into the pituitary input. The hypothalamus box is labelled: low own drive; not clamped. The pituitary box emits an ACTH pulse first; the adrenal box follows with a corticosterone pulse a little later.
scenes.narration: So in this preparation, pulsed CRH was not needed. Given a steady infusion, the pituitary and adrenal loop can make its own rhythm.
scenes.caption: So in this preparation, pulsed CRH was not needed. Given a steady infusion, the pituitary and adrenal loop can make its own rhythm.

scenes.tts: Now, where does our rule stop? In rats, learning about a place also needed the hippocampus.
scenes.visual: Edge card 1: a distinctive chamber, with the hippocampus highlighted beside the amygdala.
scenes.narration: Now, where does our rule stop? In rats, learning about a place also needed the hippocampus.

scenes.tts: A patient with selective damage to both amygdalae could still say which stimulus went with which. The learned bodily response was missing.
scenes.visual: Edge card 2: a person stating the pairing in a speech bubble; a flat autonomic-response trace beside them.
scenes.narration: A patient with selective damage to both amygdalae could still say which stimulus went with which. The learned bodily response was missing.

scenes.tts: And one breath of carbon dioxide made three women with that damage panic. That is three people, from one rare disease.
scenes.visual: Edge card 3: a single breath. Label: 3 of 3 patients panicked; 3 of 12 comparison women. Small label: one rare disease.
scenes.narration: And one breath of carbon dioxide made three women with that damage panic. That is three people, from one rare disease.

scenes.tts: Rat circuits can find necessary steps for a measured response. They cannot alone say what is felt.
scenes.visual: The three edge cards frame the map from chapter one.
scenes.narration: Rat circuits can find necessary steps for a measured response. They cannot alone say what is felt.

scenes.tts: The amygdala is needed to learn an outside threat. Neural routes respond fast; the hormone route is slower, because the adrenal must make its hormone.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: The amygdala is needed to learn an outside threat. Fast neural routes, a slower hormone route. The map has edges.
scenes.narration: The amygdala is needed to learn an outside threat. Neural routes respond fast; the hormone route is slower, because the adrenal must make its hormone.

scenes.visual: End card with the takeaway line.
